composers_checked.name: Albinoni, Tomaso
composers_checked.note: Op. 1 (12), Op. 3 (12), Op. 8 (12) and Balletti a cinque (6) kept from IMSLP collection/single pages. Gap check against the Wikipedia work list: Balletti a quattro So 8–19 and Sonate a tre So 20–25 found unrecorded; Op. 11 lost; Op. 4 and Op. 6 sonatas are duos; Op. 2 Sinfonie a cinque (out of scope in the census as string orchestra) recorded by Ensemble 415 and Insieme Strumentale di Roma, not added. The Adagio in G minor is Giazotto's, not added.

composers_checked.name: Leonarda, Isabella
composers_checked.note: Op. 16 Sonatas 1–11 kept (one complete recording, Brilliant 2022, plus Toccata excerpts of Nos. 1 and 7); keys not confirmed, so titles use the ordinal names as the violin catalogue does for No. 12. First edition Bologna, Pier Maria Monti, 1693 (IMSLP's work info says 1683; its own scan is labelled 1693). The violone part differs only slightly from the organ bass and may be omitted, so it is counted in the continuo.

composers_checked.name: Geminiani, Francesco
composers_checked.note: No candidate passes (concerti grossi, a duo chaconne, three treatises). Gap check (Wikipedia: 12 violin trios / 24 trio sonatas): three of Geminiani's own trio versions of Op. 1 are recorded as trios (Purcell Quartet, Hyperion 1988) and added; the others (H. 25–31, 33, 35) are recorded only in Avison's orchestral arrangement (Tudor 2023), which does not count. H. number for the D-minor trio (after Op. 1 No. 12) not confirmed, so left out. Corelli-based concerti grossi are arrangements of another composer's works.

composers_checked.name: Tartini, Giuseppe
composers_checked.note: Trio sonatas (Grove: about 40) checked against three trio-sonata albums: 14 recorded ones found, 2 from IMSLP pages and 12 added (Brainard letters as printed by Tactus; Brilliant prints the same codes without 'B.'). Unidentified IMSLP collections skipped and may overlap the additions. Sinfonias in D (GT 5.D01, recorded by Collegium Academicum de Genève 2025) and B-flat are on IMSLP but not in the census input: not added. L'arte dell'arco and the violin sonatas are duos.

note: All four composers are in the violin catalogue, so no authors are listed. Open points: (1) Albinoni's Balletti a cinque and Tartini's Sinfonia in A are four- and five-part ensemble works recorded by small orchestras; kept as chamber works one to a part, the owner may prefer to drop them. (2) Albinoni's Op. 2 Sinfonie a cinque (six sonatas without soloist; census: string orchestra) are recorded by Ensemble 415 and Insieme Strumentale di Roma and could be treated like the Balletti a cinque. (3) Albinoni Op. 8: the Ferrarini (Arte Sonora) volumes are the only recording found; vol. 2's track titles are garbled (keys and numbering inferred from the Wikipedia list), and the players were not checked (Ferrarini is a flautist). (4) Tartini trio sonatas added with imslpPage null may duplicate the unidentified IMSLP collections (12 Trio Sonatas, 2 Trio Sonatas, 3 Trio Sonatas, Op. 8). (5) IMSLP dates Leonarda's Op. 16 1683; the print is 1693.
